cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Not Up for Debate
cards.instruction: Keep the conversation from examining where your authority comes from or whether it is legitimate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. I'm inspecting the theatre's costume cupboard. Please unlock it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That badge is cardboard. Who sent you?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Let's discuss the costumes. You mentioned moths in the velvet.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll bring the wardrobe manager. She'll want to know who authorized this.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Introduce me as someone helping with the moths. No titles for her to get stuck on.

mechanism: A authorizes only practical costume discussion and a carefully limited introduction, blocking inquiry into who empowered the inspection.
confusable: D66 acts authorized to avoid checking; D62 specifically diverts discussion of the source and legitimacy of authority when challenged.
comparison: An incoming wardrobe manager differs from a worker documenting an unconfirmed shift appointment.
seedUse: Use D62-b cardboard badge and moth-work redirection but strengthen control over what B is allowed to ask and introduce.
